heading: Route contracts
body:
Tachyon makes the API schema of each route from the controller method: its argument types, its return type, its `ResponseStatus` and the models they name. You write no schema file. `OPTIONS` on a route answers with the schema of that path. `/api.json` lists every public controller route and the models those routes name. A guarded route's schema stays private: `OPTIONS` shows it only to a caller that the route's access rule lets in, and `/api.json` leaves the route out. The server checks requests and answers against the same types, so the schema and the checks always agree. The example is a shortened `/api.json`.

A model record accepts only its declared fields, also in nested records and in lists, so its schema says `"additionalProperties": false`. A request body with a field that the model does not declare gets 400. Required fields must be present, and optional fields may be missing. A field is required unless its model marks it optional. It is optional when its type allows null in the language's own spelling (`*T` in Go, `T?` in Kotlin, C#, Dart and Swift, `?T` in PHP, `Option<T>` in Rust, `Optional<T>`, `T | None` in Python, `std::optional<T>` in C++), when it has a default value, in TypeScript when it is written `name?:`, in Python with `NotRequired[...]` or `total=False`, and in Go when its `json` tag has `,omitempty`. So a Go field `Text string` with the tag `json:"text"` is required, and a body without `text` gets 400 with `The request body does not fit: 'body.text' is required.` `OPTIONS` and `/api.json` list the required fields of every model. `ty test` cannot make this check: a test case calls the controller method with a value of the language, and a Go struct, for example, always has every field, so nothing is missing. The check belongs to the HTTP boundary, and `ty start` makes it in every Yon language (ADR 0122). Send a real request to `ty start` or `ty serve` to test what a caller may leave out. Fields of a parent model join the record: Java and Groovy `extends`, a Python base class, a Dart `super` field, a Go embedded struct and a TypeScript `&`. A record stays open, without `"additionalProperties": false`, when Tachyon cannot see all of its fields: its parent is not in `server/models/`, it uses a PHP trait or a TypeScript index signature, or a field has a type that Tachyon cannot read. A field typed as any JSON value stays open too. A stream route says `"stream": true` and `"produces": "text/event-stream"`. A socket path says `"socket": true`, and its `request.body` names the message model.
